### 5.3 — Bash popup overflow

**Verdict**: PASS (desktop) / BLOCKED (mobile structural verification)

**Desktop (1280×720)**: Popup container right=1280px (anchored to viewport right edge), width=450px. Command element width=1065px (longer than popup), but wrapped inside depth-5 ancestor with `overflow-x: auto` (clientWidth=449, scrollWidth=1109, right=1280). Horizontal scrollbar visible inside the popup at y~437. Per acceptance rule (PASS = wrapping ancestor has overflow-x:auto/scroll AND that ancestor's right ≤ popup_right), the scroll ancestor right (1280) ≤ popup right (1280) — satisfied.

**Mobile (390 attempted)**: `browser_resize(390, 844)` did not propagate to `window.innerWidth` (remained 1280). Per prompt guidance, did not loop. Screenshot at narrower render width DID show responsive sidebar, but DOM measurements stayed at 1280px viewport. Structural mobile verification not completed.

qa_notes: Verification completed on desktop viewport. Two important observations: (1) The popup is anchored flush against the viewport right edge with R=1280 = viewport_w, leaving no margin/padding to the right. This is structurally fine but means any UI content past column 1280 is offscreen. (2) Inside the popup, the command text DOES exceed the popup's visible width but is correctly wrapped in a horizontal scroll container (overflowX:auto), which presents a small visible scrollbar in the screenshot. This matches the spec's acceptable pattern. Mobile structural testing could not be completed due to a browser viewport lock issue (the same issue the previous agent flagged) — the screenshot rendering responded to resize but JS innerWidth did not, so DOM-based PASS/FAIL on mobile could not be measured.
